title: Binary search tree
short: A tree kept in order, so each step skips half of it.
what: A binary search tree (BST) is a binary tree with one rule: everything in a node's left subtree is smaller than the node, and everything in its right subtree is bigger. To find a value you go left or right at each node, like binary search.
analogy: A "choose your path" book: at each page you pick left for smaller or right for bigger, and never read the other branch.

frames.label: BST
frames.say: Left of 8 are 3, 1 and 6, all smaller. Right of 8 are 10 and 14, all bigger. The same rule holds at every node.

frames.label: find 6
frames.say: Find 6. Start at the root, 8. 6 is smaller, so it can only be on the left. The whole right side is skipped.

frames.label: find 6
frames.say: At 3: 6 is bigger, so go right. 1 and its side are skipped.

frames.label: find 6
frames.say: Found 6 after looking at 3 nodes. In a balanced tree that is about log n looks.

frames.label: insert 9
frames.say: Insert 9 with the same walk: 9 > 8 go right, then 9 < 10 go left. 10 has no left child, so that spot is free.

frames.label: insert 9
frames.say: 9 becomes the left child of 10. Nothing else moved, and the order rule still holds.

frames.label: in-order
frames.say: Read left subtree, node, right subtree (in-order) and the values come out sorted.

when: Keep data sorted while adding and removing
Find the closest value, floor or ceiling
Validate a BST or find its k-th smallest
cost: List every value in sorted order
watch: Insert values that are already sorted and the tree becomes one long line: every step is O(n).
To validate, checking a node against its direct children is not enough. Every value on the left must be smaller.
Python has no built-in BST. For a sorted list with fast lookups use the bisect module.
